Gemini: The Phantom Ring; melancholy. “In desperate day, in hopeless night, the Phantom Ring is our last light. We yearn for power, strength and might — I seize the ring, that is my right!” 

 

Cancer: The Blue Ring; hope. “In fearful day, in raging night, with strong hearts full, our souls ignite! When all seems lost in war of light, look to the stars for hope burns bright.” 

 

Leo: The Red Ring; rage. “With blood and rage of crimson red, we fill men’s souls with darkest dread and twist your minds to pain and hate. We’ll burn you all — that is your fate!”

 

Virgo: The Ultraviolet Ring; hate. “By shield of day and shield of night, we feed and grow beyond all sight; your darkest self shall be our knight, weld the sword of unseen light!” 

 

Libra: The White Ring; life. “Live. Save. Revive. Cleanse yourself. Set your wrongs into rights. Starting from new beginnings.”

 

Scorpio: The Orange Ring; greed. “The power is mine, this is my light. Be it bright of day or black of night. I lay claim to all that falls within my sight. To take what I want, that is my right!” 

 

Sagittarius: The Gold Ring; happiness. “The golden sun will be my light, I won’t back down from a fight, I will punish the guilt, and keep the peace. I’ll fight strong, for evil never cease[s].” 

 

Capricorn: The Yellow Ring; fear. “In blackest day, in brightest night. Beware your fears made into light. Let those who try to stop what’s right burn like my power — Yellow Lantern’s might!” 

 

Aquarius: The Black Ring; death. “The blackest night falls from the skies. The darkness grows as all lights dies. We crave your hearts and your demise. By my black hand, the dead shall rise!” 

 

Pisces: The Indigo Ring; compassion. “In sorrowful day, in misfortunate night, we help those who need our might. With the lantern power, we rid your misery… with compassionate might!”

Capricorn: The Fool; a tarot card that represents starting a fresh adventure and the carefree joy of new beginnings. It’s a positive vision of trying something new and enjoying the moment.

Aquarius: Pine Cones; an essential pod that plays a role in how pine trees reproduce and continue their life cycle. A symbol of new beginnings and new life. They are a home, a shelter, and a source of food for other animals.

Pisces: The Moon; a large rock body that goes through a transformation every month, becoming a  full, all-seeing moon. The new moon is a time to set one’s intentions for good things to come in the upcoming month.

Aries: Autumn leaves; a symbol of the change that awaits a new season. The leaves turn shades of red, orange, and yellow as they fall slowly from the trees, a cycle of life and death for plants.

Taurus: Bats; a symbol of fertility as they are unique pollinators that help extend the life cycle of plants such as bananas, mangos, and agave. They are beautiful mammals that give new life to life itself as they gracefully soar across the night sky.

Gemini: Swans; the majestic, alluring birds of the lake. They start with grayish to brown feathers to blend in with the nest. The chicks soon shed their feathers and become an elegant adult swan. Swans symbolize renewal and change.

Cancer: Rabbits; a symbol of the blooming spring season, especially baby bunnies. Many baby bunnies are born when the spring flowers start to bloom. These adorable creatures showcase new life as the Earth renews itself.

Leo: Salamanders; a symbol of renewal and regeneration, as they can regrow their tails. They are associated with fire and are a symbol of transformation of its body, being born again with resistance and a stronger body.

Virgo: Ouroboros; the snake that eats itself from the tail. It comes from different cultures and spiritual beliefs around the world. It can mean infinity and self regeneration, as its body is renewed with each bite of itself.

Libra: Osiris; an Egyptian entity of Death and the Afterlife. Although he rules death and the plans of where life goes after death, he’s also a fertility god for agriculture and vegetation. He’s believed to play a role in the Nile River flooding, bringing water to vegetation and new food sources.

Scorpio: Moths; glamorous insects with a vital role in pollination, just like butterflies. Like butterflies, they transition from larvae to caterpillar to a beautiful, vibrant moth. They symbolize transformation and rebirth. 

Sagittarius: Death; a tarot card representing the metamorphosis of letting go of one’s past self and transforming into something new for the future. It’s a step into change and transformation more than the idea of death; it’s taking a step out of one’s old self into something new and improved.

Cancer: As the moon’s child, water calls to you. Make time to wade into still lakes or salty waves. Reconnect with your inner calm — it’s hiding in tide pools and late-night swims.

Leo: You shine brightest in summer, but even the sun sets. Take time to bask, not blaze. A quiet sunrise or a golden hour nap might be more fulfilling than center stage.

Virgo: Give your mind a break from to-do lists. A weekend of nothing planned is your medicine. Let the garden grow wild, the dishes wait, and your body fall into a natural rhythm.

Libra: Beauty and balance are your birthrights. Sip iced tea on a sun-dappled porch, wander through an art market, or lay on a picnic blanket with someone who gets your vibe. Summer romance isn’t always with a person — sometimes it’s with the moment.

Scorpio: This season, your transformation comes not from intensity, but from stillness. Surrender to slow mornings and starry nights. Healing isn’t always about depth — it can also live in gentle breezes and soft silence.

Sagittarius: Wanderlust is your companion, but not all adventures require a passport. Explore local trails, dance barefoot, or try a new recipe. Let joy be your compass and simplicity your guide. 

Capricorn: Hardworking as ever, you deserve a pause. Schedule in serenity like it’s your most important meeting. Mountains, cabins, or just a long bath — wherever grounds you, go there.

Aquarius: Your mind is electric, but the season calls you to reconnect with earth. Sit under a tree, cloud-watch, sketch by candlelight. The most radical thing you can do now? Rest.

Pisces: Your dreamy nature thrives in the lull of summer. Let music float through open windows and spend your afternoons drifting between daydreams. This is your season of soft magic.

Aries: Mars; the most explored planet by humans in our solar system and connected to the Roman god of war. This “red planet” is characterized by dust storms, canyons, volcanos, and polar ice caps; it’s dry, rocky, and brutally cold. There have been several missions to explore this planet to eventually get astronauts to it. The sight of the planet reminds those with a gift that winning is handed to one’s self because of the hard work one puts into their craft. Loyalty is a top priority in forming relationships. Those of this sign are true trail blazers of their own path in life; although they can be easily irritated, when one takes a look past the hard shell around them, they are truly kind and gentle souls.

Taurus: Jupiter; the largest gas planet in our solar system and connected to the Roman god of sky and thunder. The giant planet’s most obvious visual is its Great Red Spot, a huge and raging storm of pressure that’s been brewing for a century. This giant has 75 moons that circle it and a faint ring system similar to the other giant planets in our system. The presence of the striking force of thunder and the whimsy of the beautiful sky will create a magical exposure of life no one will ever experience unless one is friends with someone like this. Trustworthy, ambitious, and practical, no one is as sophisticated and dependable as a Taurus.

Gemini: Neptune; the last and furthest ice giant in our solar system and connected to the Roman god of fresh and seawater, known as Poseidon in Greek mythology. A striking, dark blue planet with faint but elegant rings that rest vertically with 14 known moons around them; it’s about 30 times as far from the sun as Earth is, unfortunately making it impossible for the naked eye to see. Yet while viewing this through other means like a telescope, it’s obvious and fascinating how someone could pass by the beauty of those who have access to this ice giant. Though sometimes overlooked, those who have the chance to be in its presence are granted with the highest level of emotional intelligence. They are great communicators and provide comfort to those who need it, but never forget that they deserve the same thing back to them: support and care.

Cancer: Haumea; the most uniquely shaped dwarf planet outside of our solar system and connected to nature, the creation of the natural world, and birth and growth of plants and animals. This meso-planet is oval/egg-shaped in nature and is the fastest rotating object in the Kuiper belt. Along with two known moons, it is the only object from the belt with rings circling its body. Though another frozen and frigid meso-planet, sensitivity and empathy will flow from the blood of those who hold the spirit of nature and creation of life. With a high level of natural intelligence, and a good sense of moral judgement, this is a true friend. Form an ever-lasting relationship with someone like this, and it will last a lifetime.

Leo: Venus; the hottest planet in our solar system and related to the Roman goddess of love, beauty, and victory. Reaching a scorching, burning temperature of 870 degrees Fahrenheit, its average surface temperature is because its atmosphere is trapping the greenhouse gases and heat from the sun on its surface. It has a diverse terrain of volcanoes, mountains, and ridged plateaus; its charming structure is shrouded in clouds of thick, toxic sulfuric acid. When viewing this planet, let the confidence surge through your veins, and continue to transfer that warmth to others that deserve it around you. Let one’s passion and artistic skills blaze a path, be proud of the work that’s been made, and show it off.

Virgo: Makemake; a dwarf planet outside of our solar system, close to Pluto and connected to the god of the Polynesian people of Easter Island, the creator of humanity and the god of fertility. It’s the largest dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, beyond Neptune, and is associated with Pluto and the rest of the dwarf planets outside. This meso-planet has a rich and harsh rose-gold to reddish-brown color as it holds chilling, frozen methane and ethane. While viewing this faraway planet, keep one’s thoughts organized and thorough to get the job done effectively and efficiently. 

Libra: Eris; a dwarf planet outside of our solar system closer to Pluto and connected to the Greek goddess of strife, chaos, and war. It’s the same size as Pluto and is similarly cold and frigid. It holds a tiny moon called Dysnomia, a symbol of this dwarf planet’s daughter, the demon goddess of unlawfulness. Although its energy of disorder and mayhem is embedded in the planet, remembering one’s own diplomatic and harmonious nature will guide one to a rich inner peace and develop deep connections with those around. Though there’s nothing wrong with dabbling in mischief and chaos once and a while for entertainment purposes, just try to be true to one’s self and make sure it’s for fun and the thrill of having a good time.

Scorpio: Ceres; a dwarf planet that lies in between the orbit of Mars and Jupiter and that is connected to the Roman goddess of agriculture. It’s the largest dwarf planet in our asteroid belt, was the first to be discovered, and is the only dwarf planet in our inner solar system. It’s fascinating that a large object like this could sit between two big planets in our own solar system, especially since the largest one is located in the asteroid belt. While looking upon this dwarf planet, let the influence of the goddess light a fire within one’s self and pave the way for one’s own path. Take care of yourself and let your authentic self shine and thrive.

Sagittarius: Saturn; a giant gas planet with gigantic beautiful rings and connected to the Roman god of time with the same name. The true prized jewel of the planet is, of course, the seven rings that wrap around it; the brilliantly bright rings shine like no other and are the most magnificent aspect of Saturn. The sight of Saturn and its gorgeous rings should put you at ease; with its guidance, time will surely be on your side for your passions and creativity. Let your own uniqueness show, and don’t be afraid to be yourself. Don’t feel any shame or embarrassment when showing one’s interests. With all of the stardust from this planet, enter into the imagination of your artistic and wonderful mind.

Capricorn: Uranus; the ice giant of the solar system and related to the Greek god of the sky, Ouranos. This planet rotates sideways and has about 13 rings around itself, the inner rings being more narrow and dark compared to the brightly colored outer rings. Its rings rest vertically, beautiful and vibrant, with 27 moons known to be orbiting around this frozen, blueish-green ball. While viewing this planet, make sure to thaw out your own heart and release any stress you may have. With the sky being your oyster, let your ambitions and dreams reach past the atmosphere and soar through the vast, ever-expanding universe. Don’t forget to take a step back, though — relax, slow down, and enjoy the small things.

Aquarius: Pluto; now a dwarf planet, is the coldest one in our solar system and is connected to the Roman god of the underworld, known as Hades in Greek mythology. This frozen ball of glaciers, mountains, and craters is truly fascinating because it has five moons, one of them about half the size of Pluto, and is called a “double planet.” When viewing this dwarf planet through a telescope, remind yourself that you are a warm and comforting soul, unlike your cold and rigid exterior. Ironically, one does not bring death like Pluto — one brings change and solidarity to ending something in one’s life and starting again. Don’t be afraid to move through challenges, and keep going to where you want to be.

Pisces: Mercury; the smallest planet in our solar system and connected to the Roman god of commerce and communication, Mercurius. Though the closest planet to the sun, it’s surprisingly cold because it does not have an atmosphere to trap the heat. The planet experiences both blazing hot and freezing cold temperatures. When this planet is visible to your naked eyes, let it be a reminder to slow down, take a breather, and stay grounded and true to yourself. Let the god of communication be your guide to form meaningful relationships — platonically, romantically, or with one’s self. Just know that your connections are valued and secure.

content.rendered:
Aries: A Ragdoll, the pretty blue-eyed, silky soft kitty cat. Their color is pretty simple, with the fur color being a tan-ish white, while the tail, ears, and spots around the face are a deeper and darker brown color. The coat of this breed is very fluffy, so this breed expects a good amount of pets and love every single day. They have a more docile and affectionate nature, so this super affectionate cat is perfect for any cat lovers out there. After all, who can say no to that cute and soft face of theirs?

Taurus: A Bengal, a very uniquely coated kitty cat right here. The spots of this breed are almost exactly the same as a jaguar’s rosette spots or its other existing patterns like spots, arrowheads, and bigger blots of marbles on its coat. This breed is actually a hybrid from crossing an Asian Leopard cat and another domestic cat, hence its distinctive coat. You are in for a real treat with this breed; it’s typically pretty friendly and playful, so get ready to tire yourself out but still have an affectionate cat that’ll love your company.

Gemini: An Abyssinian, also known as an abys, this breed has about seven fascinating, rare coat colors. These colors, from common to rarest, are ruddy (brown-orange mix), sorrel (light brown-red color mix), blue (light grey with a hint of blue), fawn (pale brown base mixed with deep pink and light brown), chocolate (richer and a bit darker kind of copper), silver (grey, blue, and tan mix), and lilac (pink and cream mix). This breed is known for being sociable in comparison to other cats, so instead of leaving them home alone for long periods of time, get another aby so they don’t get lonely, and get more toys and treats to reward them when they behave.

Cancer: A Scottish Fold, the distinct breed with a gene mutation that causes this breed’s ears to “fold” down and forward towards the front of their faces. Typical with its iconic grey coat, this breed’s behavior is really good and well-behaved, and they are more gentle, easygoing, affectionate, quiet, and playful. Not only does this gene mutation cause the folds in its ears, it’s also quite harmful for this breed because it tends to develop crippling arthritis earlier in its life. Fear not though, it can still live a healthy and normal life if you are up for taking care of it; this breed loves to cuddle, so please take good care of the breed and it’ll live a happy life.

Leo: A Siamese cat, an elegant breed of cat with beautiful dark brown markings on its face, ears, paws, and tail and a soft tan coat. This breed is known for being super playful and energetic and is great in more social situations. This breed is also very loyal, intelligent, protective, and surprisingly vocal, so they love to demand attention from their owners and are actually used as therapy cats for comfort. With their coat, they have a temperature-sensitive form of albinism, so during the winter, make sure they have a heated blanket on high at all times so they stay cuddly and comfortable under your care.

Virgo: An American Shorthair, this fierce little breed was one of the top 10 most popular pedigreed cats in the world in 2020! This breed typically comes in a grey and silver-y kind of coat littered with black blots all over its body. This breed comes in about eight different colors and patterns with more unique colors like darker blacks and browns. This breed of feline is actually descended from early European cats to help settlers protect their cargo from mice and rats! With that being said, this breed is gentle, compassionate, and are silly little guys through and through, so give them so many treats as a reward of their ancestral background!

Libra: A Persian cat, the most fluffy and chonkiest looking cat I’ve ever seen! Also known as the Persian Longhair, these cats are characterised by their round face and short muzzle, making their face even more adorable and sweet to give so many kisses to and to pet their head and face! Be careful, though, because they can develop dental problems and overgrown nails—that just means you’ll have to keep a close eye on this breed with their long coat and small face. This breed is easily adaptable, friendly, and has a sweet natured personality, so they’ll love to sit on your lap and snuggle up with you when they truly love you!

Scorpio: A Dilute Calico, the Calico already has a rare breeding rate, but the Dilute Calico is even rarer! The standard Calico breed has a one out of 1000 chance of occurring, with the Dilute Calico being even rarer than that; the dilute gene of the breed is recessive, so it has to be received from both parents in order to be born as a Dilute Calico. Standard and Dilute Calicos have a tri-color coat, but the main difference is the strength in its coat color. This specific breed of Calico’s coat is softer with its colors of gray-blue, cream, patches of white, and sprinkles of gold and silver. Count yourself very lucky with this one-in-a-million amazing Dilute Calico in your possession, keep it close, and give it all of the love it deserves in its life!

Sagittarius: A Black cat, the color as a whole is full of mystery and wonder in the feline realm. This cat’s history is filled with misconceptions, but it is actually filled with so much love, affection, and warmth towards their owner; they are the kindest and most loyal companions. Their coats can be straight jet black, smoky gray, and even a “rusting” brown color when the sunlight hits their fur just right. Their association with magic and witchcraft is perfect for the cold fall season to keep the spooky vibes but show off the adorable, loving behaviors these cats have inside. If you are lucky enough to own a black cat, that luck will certainly forever be good luck—give these cats nothing but love and care.

Capricorn: A Sphynx, the hairless yet full of love kitty cat. It’s definitely a great choice of cat if you are allergic to fur but still want a cute and adorable cat to take care of. You might have to bathe them yourself from time to time because they can easily attract dirt and dust, but they are also really good at keeping themselves just as clean as their furred brothers and sisters. This breed can actually have small, fine bristle-like hair or can be completely hairless, so make sure to give them a nice fluffy sweater to wear or keep them under a nice warm blanket. They are known for their extroverted personality with a high amount of energy, intelligence, curiosity, and affection. This breed will love to cuddle up next to you and steal your body heat while you give them a bunch of pets.

Aquarius: A Maine Coon, a large, fluffy, and social cat breed. They are known as the “gentle giant” both because of their large size and their gentle, soft, and curious behavior. They have a unique coat when it comes to adapting to their environment, but it requires minimal grooming because their undercoat actually has a double coat to help them grow a thicker coat for colder weather and a thinner one in the summer. Their water-resistant fur is longer, their long bushy tail aids them during cold wind when wrapping it around their head and shoulders, and their large paws act like snowshoes, making it easier to walk on top of snow. They are very affectionate, vocal, sociable, and intelligent, so when taking care of this breed, make sure to take them outside from time to time, and reward their good behavior with a lot of love, pets, and treats for being the “gentle giants” they are!

Pisces: A Tabby, the most “basic” cat of the feline world, yet the silliest when it comes to behavior. This cat is, surprisingly, not a breed but a coat pattern in a bunch of different species and breeds. They have a distinct “M” pattern on their forehead and stripe patterns across their eyes, cheeks, back, longs, and tail with other patterns like dots, flecks, and swirls on the other parts of the body like the chest and abdomen. They come in four distinct patterns in the gene pool: the mackerel (striped), classic or blotched (swirls), spotted (like a cheetah), and ticked (tiny dots all over the cat). Of course, since this is not breed specific, this kind of pattern is all over the place, and all over different kinds of breeds in a large variety of color and wonder. If your cat is a Tabby, give it a big kiss on its “M” marked forehead!

Leo: Stay humble in your relationships with others. Share how you feel, but don’t exaggerate.

Virgo: Try not to be so critical of yourself and your work. Lean into the process and good luck will come your way.

Aries: Hummingbirds; while impatient, you work as an individual. You are effective and ambitious in your craft and everything you do. With all that energy in their little body, hummingbirds are still gentle with their movements and actions to pursue a passionate life ahead of themselves. Passion leads to the pollination of beautiful flowers to create a better life for everyone on this Earth. Being gifted with the hummingbird guarantees a plentiful harvest for yourself and showcases the birth of something great for the foreseeable future. Don’t forget to take a break, take a deep breath, and remember to be present from time to time; your successes will be known, so keep your passion and energy high while you stop to look at what you’ve achieved with your newfound gift.

Taurus: Seeds; granting you an infinite amount of practical use and an immense amount of beauty and wonder in this lifetime. They’ll grow into anything you deserve, whether you need them as a necessity, or as something you want to look gorgeous around an ever growing garden. A beautiful flower? A long standing tree? A big pumpkin patch? Whatever it’ll grow into, the connection of the seeds and the person taking care of them is a truly dependable relationship that will bloom and blossom beyond belief. Being gifted with seeds showcases how trustworthy you are to take care of something so inherently breathtaking — a new life. Remember to be gentle: give it time and care, and don’t forget to form a bond with something you care about.

Gemini: Elephants; what curious and kind creatures they are at heart. They remember the faces of those who are the sweetest and most affectionate to them for a lifetime. They are the biggest example of gentle giants, while also being known for their dedication and wisdom. Being gifted with an elephant reminds you to be kind to yourself, just as you treat these animals; you’ve been through so much, yet you keep standing back up like these large creatures do for themselves. Give them a hug — you’ll receive the same amount of compassion back as you have ever given to anyone deserving of it in your lifetime.

Cancer: Easter Lilies; both gorgeous and a good sign of the coming: a glorious season of spring. Their bold, trumpet-like features come in pastels like whites, pinks, and yellows, yet these flowers are gentle and quiet in nature. Their intuitive ability is to negate and push away negative energy from themselves in order to thrive and foresee the growth of others in the changing season. Being gifted with these lilies might be intimidating at first. However, let this be a creative outlet for you; put some time, care, and emotions into these flowers, and they’ll continue to grow and bloom into something stunning.

Leo: The Phoenix; the embodiment of pride and boldness of one’s self. With an infinite life, no matter how heavy and how much ash remains, they rise again, and again, more beautiful and as proud as ever. Standing big and tall, this bird continues to burn with so much life; even with the amount of grief it holds, the ashes of the past blow away while the fresh, new, and better ashes stay. Being gifted with the phoenix, it’ll see the fire blazing in your soul and how courageous you are. You hold an intense amount of pride in yourself — let the flames of this gift flourish onto your own body as you hold your head up high, and don’t forget that you are as respected as this gift is to others.

Virgo: Sunflowers; these are bright and brilliant yellow flowers that always follow the sun to stay flourished and thriving. These are deeply organized flowers lined in rows next to each other, all standing tall together as the warmth of the sun shines upon their glistening petals. When being gifted with sunflowers, don’t forget to treat them with kindness — They grow fast, and their size can be towering compared to you, but don’t worry, do the research to care for these flowers, and they’ll be the results of your kindness. Don’t worry about them too much, though, for they are sturdy; use the time while your sunflowers are growing to heal and rest. It’s still important to do something fun with yourself and some close friends.

Libra: Rainbows; the lovely aftermath after a rainstorm with a shining sun. With an unbelievable array of pastels, these colors are from the well-known color wheel many artists have learned from — how someone could not stop and look at this wonderful natural phenomenon is beyond comprehension. Coming in beauties like in doubles or singles, glories, or halos, it’s truly a gift nature can happily create in one’s lifetime. Being gifted with rainbows, it makes a statement about one’s natural beauty and how glorious it is to be alive at a time when a rainbow is showing. With the variety of colors to see, you can get some inspiration with what to create when the time is right — but don’t forget to still put yourself first and keep yourself shining.

Scorpio: Butterflies; what fragile and gentle insects they are. Coming in a variety of colors and forms from all around the world, it’s still amazing to see these creatures in your life when one is going through change themselves. Starting small in a world so big around them, crystalizing themselves for safety and comfort, then metamorphosing into the most pleasing and alluring creatures on Earth to take on life with such joy and wonder. They don’t know what’s ahead of them, but they still keep flapping their wings as they travel from flower to flower: collecting nectar, spreading pollen, and keeping the ecosystem alive and thriving. When gifted with butterflies, you might stay in your own shell at first, but with time and a lot of protection, you’ll crawl out. The pure enthusiasm experienced through these insects is a reminder how important it is to change and how scary it can be at first — helping you tremendously.

Sagittarius: Shooting Stars; a delightful shower of a faraway sun, zooming past the chill of the night sky. Don’t forget to close your eyes and make a wish — no matter how big or small it is. It may even come true in your lifetime; but don’t keep your eyes closed for long because you might see more stars flying across the night sky. Brilliant and exciting balls of space matter, and elements that turn into the suns of other solar systems in the vastness of space. Shooting stars are quite a sight to see. When being gifted with shooting stars, let them fly however you want, be as creative as possible, and make sure they shine as bright as your soul. Although you like to be solo, try to surround yourself with people that let you be adventurous, like stars travelling together.

Capricorn: Sunrises; a start of a new day — a well deserved one. The warmth of the sun’s rays hitting your face, reminding you how wonderful the day is going to be; look at that view. No matter where you are, the sun will always shine a ray to somewhere beautiful; one’s pets, one’s room, the outside, oneself, anywhere the light wants to be showcased. When the sun rises, let the light wash upon you while the day begins, whether one is an early bird getting ready as soon as the sun peeks out, or a night owl sleeping in on a glorious day. Being gifted with sunrises, you’ll naturally follow the routine of a new day: bright, early, carefree, and ready to take on anything. Don’t forget that it’s okay to not perfectly follow a pattern. Let the coziness of the sun’s rays keep you grounded in the present, and make sure to sit down and get a sweet treat for yourself.

Aquarius: Lotus Flowers; a sacred and graceful flower that holds the most amount of beauty. With gorgeous, pastel, pink petals that grow on lily pads, these flowers are the embodiment of enlightenment and peace. These flowers open themselves to those who desire to look upon their beauty. They surround themselves with other blooming flowers, and peacefully float in a clear, and flourishing ecosystem. Being gifted with the lotus flower reminds you to stop and practice serenity. The drive to evolve yourself is admirable, but don’t forget to not get lost in your idealistic ways. Your work shows growth; tranquility is key.

Pisces: Waterfalls; a stunning key to a rich, aquatic ecosystem. The sounds of water crashing down onto rocks below, and the mist spraying onto the skin of those close to the falls is quite a breathtaking sight to see for whoever is interested in seeing this formation from nature. A representation of cleansing and renewal. The water constantly flows, purifying the body, mind, and souls of those who seek it out themselves — free from any negative energy. When being gifted with waterfalls, don’t be afraid to let your emotions flow, and allow yourself to feel. Let your tears fall, and let your body cleanse itself as waterfalls do. It’s healthy, and it’s just as natural as any other emotion that enters your mind and soul. Be kind to yourself, and continue to be creative with your art. Showcase yourself, with that artistic and intricate mind of yours.

Aries: Have you gone on a walk lately? Going to class doesn’t count. Embrace the milder weather this week with a stroll through the Natural Lands, explore Norway Valley (underrated!), or venture out into Northfield. The only requirement is to walk aimlessly, yet purposefully.

 

Taurus: You’re strong and confident like a bull, but you don’t keep that same energy when it comes to cultivating your relationships. Dive horns first into asking someone out this week, or hit up a friend you’ve been meaning to hang out with. 

 

Gemini: Play a classic online game that you used to love. Options include, but are not limited to, slither.io, 2048, or Papa’s Freezeria. It may not seem productive, but it’s better than scrolling on Instagram Reels. Sorry. 

 

Cancer: Streeetchhhh! Literally just for 5 minutes. Reach for the sky, crack your knuckles, hit a tree pose — whatever your jam is. You’ll feel so much better afterwards. 

 

Leo: Order your favorite Cage drink and sit pensively in a window seat. It could fix all of your problems, but we can’t guarantee anything.

 

Virgo: Clean out that drawer you keep closed to avoid confronting. Even if you can’t see the mess, it’s still there. 

 

Libra: Get a new tattoo or piercing. Considering that Kinship Collective was actually recently nominated for Star Tribune’s Minnesota’s Best award for a Tattoo and Piercing Shop, now’s the time if you’ve been thinking about it.

 

Scorpio: Get your friends together and tell them a really, really big secret. 

 

Sagittarius: Take out a notebook or a piece of paper and write down 10 things you are grateful for. 

 

Capricorn: Compliment someone you think is really cool, even if you don’t talk to them that much. Dearest Capricorn, while it’s admirable to stay in your lane and keep your focus, it also pays to show people kindness. 

 

Aquarius: Tell someone in your life about a song you really like. See if they like it too.

 

Pisces: Schedule an appointment with the Counseling Center.

Capricorn   

You’re an Elf! I am so sorry that you’re about to be summoned to the North Pole to help build some toys. Enjoy your time on campus while you can!

Aquarius 

You’re a Nymph! Take a break from your homework and take some time to frolic near Heath Creek.

Pisces 

You’re a Narwhal! Yeah. Maybe narwhals exist. But so do you. What a joy it is that you exist! Go give a hug to someone you love. 

Aries  

You’re a Fairy! You flutter your sweet little wings over to the Cage and buy yourself a little sweet treat, just because you deserve it.

Taurus 

You’re a Minotaur! You’re strong and wonderful. Also know that you can still be strong and wonderful, while also opening up. You’re allowed to be sensitive.

Gemini 

You’re a Leprechaun! Get that bag. Also remember to make some time for what matters most to you. Which may be precious coins. But make something up, like friends, if that’s the case. 

Cancer 

You’re a Pegasus! Go for a walk this week, and let the breeze fly through your feathers and remind you of the woods from which you came from.

Leo 

You’re a Unicorn! Well aren’t you just magical. Flaunt that outfit sometime this week. You will look stunning.

Virgo 

You’re a Centaur! You’re graceful and swell. You will carry out your finals week with grace. Take some time for yourself too, because finals week isn’t as graceful as you make it work.

Libra 

You’re a Siren! Consider not dragging people into the depths of the sea, but just do your 

homework. This week, you’re going to ace that presentation, and look great doing it. 

Scorpio 

You’re a Phoenix! Finals week will be a breeze for you, so don’t stress. Go ahead and prepare to spread your wings and fly. 

Sagittarius

You’re a Gnome! Go grab a blanket, get cozy. It’s been a long week, so go ahead and take your time. Take a nap. The world is yours.

Aquarius: Mental health days are only supposed to last one day btw. Please do your homework.

Pisces: When was the last time you called your mom? Went on a walk? You can’t hide away forever.

Aries: You need to start giving yourself credit where it’s due! You’re doing a good enough job, even if it feels like everything is falling apart. 

Taurus: Stop doubting yourself and your abilities!!!

Gemini: You won’t get anything done if you keep procrastinating and comparing yourself to everyone else! You need some self-love, friend.

Cancer: If you’ve been thinking they aren’t the one for you, you’re probably right, and it’s time to accept that. 

Leo: The only way to gain control is to start looking inward. Reflect on what you could’ve done better, and then improve!

Virgo: If everything feels like it is falling apart, it’s time to do something about it! Things will get better if you give yourself a chance. 

Libra: A trip to a rage room would do you wonders, and maybe even a trip to the Wellness Center

Scorpio: Failure is just part of creativity! Embrace it.

Sagittarius: You keep acting out of impulse and then wondering why things go wrong!!! Think before you act, pretty please.

content.rendered:
Capricorn   

Do not be afraid of changes that happen, but don’t let them influence all of your actions. Trust your intuition and things will work themselves out.

Aquarius 

 Stop avoiding your problems! While they grant you small relief now, it’s not worth it in the long run — even if you’re scared. Face what’s in front of you. It’ll lead to good things!

Pisces 

Your streak of good luck is coming to an end soon. Embrace your failures!! Living in fear of them will only make it worse. Embrace your mistakes and messes, but most of all, be kind to yourself when they happen.

Aries  

Someone in your life is hurting you! They may be talking about you behind your back. This may be someone very close to you! It will be scary to let them go, but it may be for the best. 

Taurus 

It’s time to get your act together! Clean your room!! You can’t neglect yourself forever, it’s not going well. It’s time for a confidence boost, and to do your homework!!!

Gemini 

 Allow yourself to love!!! Your anxiety is getting the better of you and it’s time to let that go. Good things are coming, but only if you work for them.

Cancer 

The universe thanks you for cutting them off (if you haven’t yet, do so now). It’s time for new beginnings! Things are about to start going your way. 

Leo 

That job is not worth it!!! And it’s time to start looking inwards.Maybe the things going wrong are actually your fault! It’s okay if they are. 

Virgo 

Life will be so good once you end that situation. Maybe try some meditation!

Libra 

It’s okay to be a bit overwhelmed right now! You’re doing all you can. Go for walks, watch the sunset, maybe start saying affirmations.

Scorpio 

Go to your professor’s office hours!!! Your grade depends on it.

Sagittarius

Text them. I know!!! Insane!! But if you’re not satisfied with how it ended, there might be a reason why. You deserve love and security!!

content.rendered:
Aries: Chocolate Chip Cookies; there’s nothing wrong with a simple and delicious bucket of cookies to eat while you enjoy yourself at the State Fair. With the gooey-ness of chocolate and the overall softness of the cookie itself, it’s a great choice to have at a carnival as well. Be proud of the fact that you are an all-time favorite versatile dessert. 

Taurus: Elote; the main ingredients are roasted corn with crema, cotija cheese, lime, chili powder, and tahini. It’s a great meal you can eat on a stick or in a nice little cup while you enjoy the flavor of the corn itself. It’s truly delicious if you want to try something new or eat something you are very familiar with. This is an amazing choice at a fair or carnival. 

Gemini: Dole Whip; typically a pineapple-flavored sweet treat, yet it also comes in strawberry, lime, as well as mango-garnished tajin and chamoy with an added tamarind candy straw found specifically at the State Fair from the Tasti Whip stand. It’s an all-time sweet and chill treat to cool yourself down on a hot summer day — whether you choose to taste every single flavor to see which is your favorite, or you sit down with the standard, yet delightful, pineapple flavor of this treat. 

Cancer: Churros; a sugary and filling treat one should eat at a fair or carnival. It’s a staple fried food with delicious cinnamon sugar and topped with chocolate sauce, caramel sauce, or a mix of both when being served. It is a simple, yet mouthwatering dish that one would be happy to buy while having a blast winning games and riding rides. Nothing about churros should be passed if you want to be filled and satisfied. 

Leo: Soft Pretzels; served fresh and ready-to-go, soft pretzels are simply a delicious kind of food you can buy cheap, which also comes with salt and melted cheese for added flavor. Whether you buy them small or served large, anyone would want to take a bite and have a taste for themselves. A soft pretzel with a delicious beverage can make any day out and about at the fair or carnival a satisfying and delicious day. 

Virgo: Snow Cones; the simplest treat one can buy on a hot and eventful day. Snow cones can come in any kind of flavor imaginable. The most memorable syrups of a snow cone include: blue raspberry, cherry, root beer, and cola. A cold treat can go a long way to chill yourself down and still make your stomach happy with the simple flavors of this shaved ice. 

Libra: Funnel Cakes; specifically found at carnivals, this deep-fried batter in no particular shape nor size comes with powdered sugar and an assortment of fruits like strawberries and blueberries. It is another staple among fried carnival foods in the carnival and fair realm. This is another delicious and filling food one could eat while you walk around the fairgrounds and enjoy yourself there. 

Scorpio: Caramel Apples; simply apples on a stick rolled in a layer of caramel, usually covered with nuts, sprinkles, or small savories. It’s definitely a simple treat, yet, it’s a rewarding one when it’s served cooled and can be deliciously satisfying with the sweetness of the caramel and the sourness of the green apple. 

Sagittarius: Deep-Fried Oreos; a delicious Oreo cookie dipped in batter, deep-fried, and sprinkled with powdered sugar. Served in bunches in a small basket when served warm, nothing beats the taste of a nice, tasty Oreo with the added flavor of powdered sugar and deep-fried batter. It’s a biased pick for myself, yet, I would bet that others also enjoy this treat. It is a tasty treat and can be replicated at home. Similar to all of the other treats, it’s definitely something you could enjoy while staying at a carnival or fair grounds. 

Capricorn: Fried Pickles; a savory and delicious pickle, specifically found at the State Fair again, that can be served regularly with spicy cajun seasoning or with cream cheese in the middle, while typically served with ranch or hot sauce. With the variety of different flavors and with the option of a non-fried giant pickle on a stick, it’s a great savory snack to walk around with. 

Aquarius: Lemonade; the most iconic and popular drink you could have while walking around and wanting to stay hydrated compared to water. Ranging from regular yellow lemonade to pink lemonade, with the correct amount of sugar, water, and lemon juice, it’s definitely the most enjoyable drink one can have — that’s non alcoholic — and something that’ll make one happy and nostalgic. 

Pisces: Cotton Candy; a delicious mouthful of sugar that’s for everyone. It is a treat that is super sweet and versatile in shape where one can make it look like anything imaginable. Typically found in flavors including pink vanilla and blue raspberry, it’s something easy and very nice to eat. Although it’s easily sticky, it’s worth it when you can always either share it with others or happily eat it by yourself.

Aries

Lean into the natural impulsivities of being the first sign — and a fire sign, too — in the zodiac! Try costume-shopping with no idea of what to go as, buying candy not originally on your grocery list, or trying a new, fall-themed drink downtown.

Taurus

Revel in the simple things this Halloween — as an Earth sign, relish in the practical simplicities of the holiday, like the act of getting dressed with friends, the fiery, autumnal colors of the trees, or an apple cinnamon muffin from the Cage.

Gemini

Enjoy the sociability that comes with the holiday. Ask your friends to watch a horror movie on the fifth floor of Holland, or share scary stories in your dorm room. Whatever you do, do it with people you love.

Cancer

Take personal joy in the rituals that come with Halloween. Enjoy the act of putting up decorations, deciding on costumes, and drinking good apple cider. Treat yourself with experiences that matter.

Leo

Lean into your creative side. Go as a niche character this Halloween and embrace the opportunity to talk about them; come up with a new recipe and make it tradition to cook; write or draw or portray somehow your favorite scary story.

Virgo

Try a practical and nostalgic costume this year — if you haven’t ordered yours already. Go as something you loved from your childhood or redo a costume you did as a child and enjoy the way it feels to do it again, this time older, as your current self.

Libra

Ask your friends to see who can come up with or share the scariest creature-centered story. Enjoy the way the stories might quickly derail or build upon each other, take the opportunity to make new inside jokes with one another, and despite the original goal of scaring, see whose story ends up the most ridiculous.

Scorpio

Despite how busy this time of year is, try and find ways to say “yes” to things — a party, a costume, a dinner with friends in Stav, or a day downtown. The time and energy you put into the things you accept will come back to you.

Sagittarius

Embrace the spontaneity of your sign: show up to Halloween in an elaborate costume, make a late-night trip to the Pause, or fall down creepy Wikipedia rabbit holes. Do what you want and enjoy yourself all the while.

Capricorn

Be authentic with yourself and others this time of year — if your favorite candy is Tootsie Rolls, mention it, and if you don’t like candy corn, say so. Share what’s on your mind, but share it truthfully and openly.

Aquarius

Think past the holiday and make sure you’re on top of things before celebrating Halloween however you might. Relish in the organization of finishing homework before it’s due and having less work than usual over a holiday weekend.

Pisces

Enjoy the nostalgia that comes with the holiday — enjoy what’s familiar and embrace what’s not, or try embracing the two. Take part in one of your family’s Halloween traditions while participating in something new on campus.

Aries – Do y’all ever get the feeling that you’re just a less cool Capricorn? A ram’s basically just a goat, but just… not as rad. That’s what the stars think, anyway.

Taurus – Mars is in ascendancy today. As in the candy company. Their stock was up 2.11% when the market closed.

Gemini – Why are you guys the only star sign to get two? The other stars don’t think that’s fair, so they’ll be cutting one of the twins into 12 equal pieces and splitting them between you all. From now on you will be 1 & 1/12 twin.

Cancer – Your namesake is trying to kill you. Today’s a good day to visit the oncologist!

Leo – You guys just think you’re so cool, don’t you? You’re so much better than us, with your lion. Let’s see if you still feel that way after 10/20/2023.

Virgo – Your lucky numbers today are whatever you want them to be! Except 9. Stay. Away. From. 9.

Libra – Yeah, she’s the one, girl. Unless you really don’t like her, in which case ignore the stars and break up with her. They don’t know you like you do!

Scorpio – You know what you did. And pretty soon, all of them will too. Your countdown to ruination is ticking away, Scorpio.

Sagittarius – I can’t believe you said that on Twitter three years ago, Sagittarius! That was just… such a shit take.

Capricorn – Don’t forget, Capricorn. Midnight on Saturday, behind the CVS. Bring the Enucleator.

Aquarius – You’re lookin fly today, Aquarius! It’s a real day to put yourself out there, at least for like an hour before you realize you left your phone in the dorm and dejectedly return to it. Maybe tomorrow…

Pisces – You’re doing so well today! Everyone thinks you’re great, and you’re growing into exactly the young woman you want to be. The stars love you.

Virgo: 

You will feel a strong affinity and sense of empathy for the Northern Pike this week. Try and avoid going fishing if you can, and if you do go, make sure to catch-and-release. Step carefully around such potential for emotional turmoil.

 

Aries: 

On a Thursday in the near future, you will find yourself in a BP gas station, and you will feel incredibly hungry. Do not purchase the jalapeno bratwurst, no matter how delicious it may seem.

 

Capricorn:   

The water from the west-wing drinking fountain on the fourth floor of the library will taste especially delicious on May 3. Make sure to fill up a bottle and enjoy.

 

Cancer: 

When you reach the age of 42, the likelihood that you will lose your right index finger increases by roughly 35 percent for the duration of that year. I have no insight as to how or why your probability of losing said finger increases, but do with that prediction what you will.

 

Pisces: 

Do not attempt to do a standing backflip this week. You’re very athletic, and I know you’ve been practicing, but it just won’t end well this week. Stay safe, lie low, try it again next week.

 

Sagittarius: 

Wear a rain jacket tomorrow, no matter what the weather looks like. You will encounter an Australian Naval Captain who will be impressed by your preparedness and offer you a position as an Admiral. Heed this call to adventure at your own discretion.

 

Taurus: 

Be aware of the Taurus man. This coming week, he will fall in love with you. Though not a Taurus himself, he is seductive and he will insistently ask you to accompany him on a date to Seaworld. Do not go on this date with him. If you do, you will fall madly in love with him, and he will break your heart.

 

Gemini:  

On May 7, 2023, purchase a plane ticket to Winnipeg, Canada. From there, contract a local bush pilot named “Scruff” for a flight that takes you as close to the coordinates 64.615446, -83.704826 as you can get. From there, proceed on foot. Good things will follow.

 

Leo: 

The Olaf Messenger has informed me that due to contract obligations, I am not allowed to disclose your horoscope at this time. I hope you have an excellent day, though.

 

Scorpio: 

You will find yourself in a moment of complete boredom for approximately 30 minutes next Wednesday. However, it will provide you with exactly enough time to read Nikolai Gogol’s classic short story, “The Nose.” Make sure to bring along a printout of this story, because it will brighten your day and make that moment of boredom pass easily.

 

Aquarius:

You will have a soul-crushing, mind-melting, life-altering love affair with someone for the next few months. Congratulations! However, their name will only be revealed to you via an innocuous, automatically generated email. Make sure you check your spam folder in the coming weeks very carefully, and don’t be afraid to reach out!

 

Libra: 

 A mild pipeline maintenance incident occurred April 22, 2023 somewhere on the Pacific Coast of Canada. This mild mishap will cause gas prices to increase by roughly .0045 percent by April 29, precisely when you will go to fill up your car. Make sure to pack a few extra pennies.

content.rendered:
Masks have become a part of everyday style here on campus. The one you pick out each morning might match your mood or your outfit, or it may be a rushed decision when you’re late for class. Though St. Olaf provided all students with masks, many homemade or individually purchased masks roam around campus each day. Here are just a few of those, and what their owners have to say about them:

“My mom brought this mask to me from the kitchen store she works at. I like it because it has flowers on it, and I like flowers.” — Brennan Brink ’21


“This one’s reversible!” — Freya Gordon ’24

“We got these ones from Target.” — Emma Borkowski ’21
“I think it really brings out my eyes.” — Gretchen Olson ’21

“You want me to say something about my mask?!” — Sam Bailey ’21

“I love this mask because it’s sustainably made with salvaged hemp! Go green!” — Reilly Friend ’24

“It’s laundry day for my masks!” — Solveig Gordon ’21

So, whether you’re tossing your mask in the laundry, or you’ve got on your absolute favorite, wearing your mask is what counts! Thanks for masking up, St. Olaf, and let’s continue to see all those unique face coverings around campus so that everyone can express themselves while staying safe!

content.rendered:
Last of the Long Lost
In every raided grave of dreams,
Lies a wreath of hope.
In every torn, tattered and shattered spirit,
The soul and the bones do hold.
From the blanket of the winter snow,
From crevices stuffed with horrors untold,
A fragile rose dares to grow.
For these are fires that hoses cannot quench,
They just surge up, can’t turn, won’t relent.
These are voices that a thousand rifles and muzzles
Can never muffle, feathers that just won’t ruffle.
And so, up from a distant corner in the dark,
Up from a valley darker than a prison yard,
Up from the rubble emerges a figure all so stark
He shakes off the night’s pitch black cloak
Till his eyes burn brighter than a fire well stoked.
He is beaten black and blue,
Pound and pommeled, left all bruised.
But the infinite loop of turmoil couldn’t finish him off,
From the ashes he rose like a phoenix aloft.
For out of the darkness a star was born-
A rose that grew from amongst the thistles and thorns.
With awe, all the world turned to see,
And said please do tell
Who are you that still stands where many men fell?
And he said, ‘I am the last of the long lost,
Son of the long gone,
The seed watered with tears and blood,
Defying the scorching searing heat of the summer’s sun,
The birth of a dream and a promise of what’s to come.
Living up to my forefathers’ creed
Sparking life to their visions and dreams
AYE, I AM THE LAST OF A DYING BREED!’

Earlier this fall semester, St. Olaf Choir Conductor and Harry R. and Thora H. Tosdal Professor of Music Dr. Anton Armstrong announced his retirement after the 2027-2028 academic year. Armstrong inherited his conductor position in 1990 from his mentor Kenneth Jennings, making him the fourth in the choir’s history. Armstrong is known for transforming the choir, incorporating African American spirituals and being a creative director for the St. Olaf Christmas festival.

The Olaf Messenger sat down with Armstrong for a one-on-one Q&A about his retirement, hope for the future of the choir and reflections on his life and career.

Q: What are your plans for retirement?

A: I thought about this for a while, and I’m at peace with this decision. I’ve seen a lot of changes … When I was appointed to the position, I inherited a very healthy musical organization, the same choir, from my predecessor, my mentor, Kenneth Jennings. And that’s how I hoped to leave it to the next person who succeed[s] me. People don’t replace people. They succeed people … Each conductor opened new doors for what the St. Olaf Choir would do in terms of repertoire but also what they would do in terms of their services, community and the wider world.

Q: This is your 37th year with the choir. You’ve traveled the world; you’ve been to Australia, South Africa, and Japan, just to name a few. What does Norway being your last international tour mean to you?

A: Well, it’s my bookend. It was my first international tour in 1993. So it will bookend my career here. But the city is always beautifully adorned … The people are really wonderful. They have welcomed immigrants to their country, but they’ve done it in a wise way, in a welcoming way.

Yes, we’ve had this tie to Norway because of our founding by Norwegian immigrants. And in my position as the conductor of St. Olaf Choir, I have been privileged to encounter the royal family, especially the late king. I’ve encountered him five different times in my life … When you were in his presence, he made you feel like the most important person in the world. I want to show you a quick picture.

[Armstrong then pulled out his phone, showing a picture of the late King Harald V and himself.]

Q: What moments throughout your career specifically have stood out to you?

A: Well, I guess I have my friends from my grad school days. Right after I finished at St. Olaf, I went to the University of Illinois (Urbana-Champaign). One of my dearest and oldest friends from [University of Illinois], Scott Andre Thomas, who for many years had the choral music program at Florida State University … has become an associate artist of the London Symphony Orchestra. He would say that when we were students, I had a dream to come back here and be the conductor of [the St. Olaf] choir. I didn’t say that to too many people because I never thought St. Olaf would hire me. I was 33 when I got this job, so I was very young … I did my dissertation on the St. Olaf Choir, so I knew this place … I’ve tried to expand the repertoire that would find a place for me, the wider church of God … I’m also the artistic director of the Christmas festival, and that’s, to me, a very powerful statement of St. Olaf as a community of faith … I think what we try to do here has to be done. Christianity in this country especially has been hijacked by people. And I think St. Olaf can stand as a canon light of God’s love and God’s gratitude to all people — race, gender, sexual orientation, and identity.

Q: What do you wish for the future of St. Olaf Choir?

A: Well, I’ll say something about the choir, but also the College. I’m very proud of how this school has risen in how people understand it as a place of academic excellence. I know the three prongs we stand on, liberal arts education, global encounter, but don’t forget we are a community of faith that welcomes people of non-faith, and it gives us distinction … But at the heart, [we] are a college built out of the Christian faith. And as I said, in the best of Christianity, we are welcoming … God created people who will love songs and write ballads so that we can continue … I hope the person who [succeeds me] will recognize the responsibility to continue to preach a gospel of love and peace, and it doesn’t have to be just sacred music — it can be done with music outside of church music … A search for excellence for me personally is the highest expression of praise I give back to the Creator who gave me this.

On July 31, St. Olaf College administrators received an email from Dr. Mark J. Perry alleging discrimination in the College’s summer STEMQuest Flash Camp, a camp advertised for “rising sixth-through-ninth grade girls.” In his email, Perry claimed that due to the “no-boys-allowed” nature of the camp, St. Olaf had violated federal law under Title IX. Perry further notified administrators that he would thereby file a federal civil rights complaint against the College.

While most present-day Title IX litigation typically revolves around harassment and sexual misconduct within school programs, Perry’s complaint emphasized Title IX’s participation-focused aspects. Under the law, educational programs and activities are ineligible to receive federal funding if they exclude or otherwise discriminate against students based on sex. In his complaint, Perry gave the College the option to either “(1) termin[ate] the female-only Camp in question, (2) open the Camp in the future to all students regardless of sex, or (3) introduc[e] an equivalent boy-only STEMQuest Summer Camp that would equitably and legally accommodate all middle school students interested in STEM regardless of sex.” The College chose the second option upon the guidance of General Counsel and Vice President for Human Resources Carl Crosby Lehmann ’91. 

Filing federal civil rights complaints against colleges and universities for alleged Title IX violations is nothing new for Perry. A retired economics professor who taught at the University of Michigan-Flint for 25 years, Perry has filed over 1,200 similar complaints to numerous institutions — in almost every case highlighting alleged discrimination against boys and young men. Yet Perry does not consider himself to be a “reverse discrimination” activist. 

In a letter to the editor Perry submitted to the “Duke Chronicle,” Perry claimed that because women are “53% of Duke undergraduates,” his federal complaint regarding a scholarship Duke offered only to women was actually an effort to protect a minority group — men.

Some Title IX experts are skeptical of Perry’s use of Title IX. In an interview with Bridge Michigan, Senior Director of Safe and Inclusive Schools at the National Women’s Law Center Shiwali Patel claimed that Title IX does allow for schools to have gender-conscious programming, of which the STEMQuest Flash Camp would be an exemplar. 

“Schools have been able to create policies aimed at increasing the participation of women and girls in fields where they are underrepresented,” Patel said. Perry’s efforts to use Title IX against policies such as these, she argued, are “troubling.”

Aca Ajkoviq ’27, a mathematics and physics major, agrees with Patel’s characterization. “Who are we giving the unfair advantage to?” Ajkoviq asked in an interview with The Olaf Messenger. “I don’t see it.” 

Although Ajkoviq claims she was “lucky enough to have an established desire to pursue science since [she] was eight years old,” she pointed out that even she “started questioning things” when she saw the gender makeup of many of her STEM classes in high school. For Ajkoviq, the purpose of the STEMQuest Flash Camp was to correct systemic problems surrounding gender imbalances in STEM. According to Ajkoviq, the STEMQuest Flash Camp gave middle school girls the opportunity to “create a community … from the very beginning,” counteract common problems such as self-doubt and develop their skills in a non-judgmental space. Ajkoviq went on to say that if Perry “truly cared about sex discrimination,” he would be focusing on increasing training for schoolteachers to “address gender divides.”

Activists like Perry, however, remain unconvinced. For Perry, the fact-of-the-matter was that because St. Olaf was offering a program that restricted an activity to just girls without offering boys a similar program, the College was breaking the law and jeopardizing its federal funding. For Perry, “hav[ing] good intentions” or giving an advantage to the ‘right’ sex for the ‘right reasons’” were not valid excuses. While the College did eventually heed to Perry’s warnings and subsequent complaint by making the camp co-ed, students like Ajkoviq maintain that St. Olaf made the wrong decision. She said, “the fact that [St. Olaf administration] buried their head in the stand on this gives me way less trust and respect for them.”

Q: What position are you right now on football and track? 

A: I’m in a position where I essentially had to medically retire from football, and I’m now competing in track and field. I will be doing shot put and hammer throw this upcoming season. 

 

Q: How long have you been playing football? 

A: I started football in high school, so I did that for about seven years. I did pretty well my senior year [and] committed to St. Olaf. [I] came in with an ACL tear, so I basically had to just rehab [until] sophomore year. Junior year, I started to experience some back problems [and] discovered I had degenerative disc disease. Over the summer, I was doing some sprints and experienced a hamstring tear. So, we called in and told the coaches: “Hey, it’s looking like it’s towards the end of my football career.” However, I talked to the track and field coach, and he’s giving me a spot with track and field. I’ll be doing shot put and hammer throw this upcoming season.

 

Q: What’s a piece of advice/words of wisdom that you would pass down to future players? 

A: Track wise, do what you got to do. Keep working, essentially do what’s best for you, being able to compete at a level that these other guys are competing on. Football, like I said, I feel like it’s way more competitive. That’s dog-eat-dog there, you got to do your business. But on top of that, be able to have an edge on other people in your position. Have edges for some of these opposing teams you may play during your seasons. Like I said, do what your coach says, be consistently great at what you do, and provide some type of winning edge outside of what’s required. You should be a damn good player. Student-wise, use your resources. I believe that using your resources, being able to talk to some of the other students in your major, in your classroom, some of the professors, administrators. Everyone’s going to help you out, they want the best for you. 

 

Q: As you’re entering your senior year, what’re you going to miss about St. Olaf? What were small moments you enjoyed during your time as a student?

A: It’s been a great experience for me, really. I feel like some personal outliers may have thrown me off a bit, but I feel like it was a family here [and] on the football team here. [And] some family on the track team. They’ve been wanting me to come and compete with them for a while now, I just didn’t have the time to essentially execute what I was trying to do for them. So, I’m doing what I can now.

content.rendered:
Family Weekend is coming up on Oct. 2 to 4. With only a few days to show your family around Northfield, here are five places and activities to add to your itinerary. 

Content Bookstore

Located in downtown Northfield, Content Bookstore is great for readers of all ages. Families can spend time perusing the shelves and looking through the store’s recommendations for their next read. Content does not only offer books — there is also a large selection of puzzles, crafts and games. There is even a large toy section for any younger family member.

Content is open Monday through Wednesday and Friday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Thursdays 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sundays 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Tin Tea

Opened by St. Olaf alum Chau Truong ’24, Tin Tea is a great place to stop in for a refreshing boba drink and fresh food, including spring rolls and bánh mì. From 8 p.m. to 10 p.m., they host a happy hour with $5 drinks. The store recently introduced its fall menu, which contains drinks like the Pumpkin Cookie Butter Cà Phê and Caramel Apple Booster. “We try our best to collaborate with as many local farms and businesses as we can when we release each menu,” Truong said in an interview with The Olaf Messenger. This year, they partnered with Trump’s Orchard. 

Tin Tea is open Tuesday through Sunday 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

Hideaway

For a coffee break or for lunch, head to The Hideaway Coffeehouse and Wine Bar in downtown Northfield. Its menu contains a wide range of coffee and tea, and food such as breakfast items, salads, sandwiches and paninis — including the St. Olaf 2.0 panini with chicken, tomato, arugula, onion, brie and pesto. The restaurant also sources many ingredients locally. It’s the perfect, cozy spot for a warm cup of coffee or tea on a fall day. 

Hideaway is open Friday through Tuesday 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Wednesday through Thursday 7 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. 

Thrifting

Thrifting is a popular activity among students, and Northfield has several options for families interested in vintage shopping. Clothes Closet, The Thrifty Parrot and The Bearded Mermaid offer consignment clothing. The Boho Peacock is a secondhand clothing store filled with hand-selected, stylish clothing and jewelry. Vintage Etc. and Fate Vintage carry collectibles, antiques, clothes and more. Fate Vintage also has a wide selection of charms to add to Italian charm bracelets. 

Cannon River

The Cannon River runs through Northfield and has surrounding trails to explore the area. The East River Trail is a 2.6 mile paved path connecting Dundas and downtown Northfield for hikers and bikers. Families can also walk Carleton College’s arboretum trails, which follow the Cannon River and pass through the forest. In early October, the trails show off Minnesota’s fall colors. 

Beyond these activities, families can take the time to walk around downtown and discover the local businesses that make Northfield special. 

Truong said the community’s support has been important to her experience as a business owner. “Northfield’s people are so ready to support any small business, which is really special.”

Alyssa Melby, director of the St. Olaf Svoboda Center for Civic Engagement, launched a write-in campaign for the Northfield Public Schools Board of Education on Aug. 19. After four candidates filed for three open seats during the candidate filing period, two withdrew from the race, leaving a vacant seat. To fill the vacancy, Melby must receive enough write-in votes, which Northfield residents cast by printing her name on the ballot. If Melby’s write-in campaign is successful, the board will avoid appointing a member to serve temporarily, in accordance with Minnesota law. 

Melby has toyed with the idea of serving on the school board, having been asked to run in 2024, but until now, it wasn’t the right time. With incumbents Ben Miller and Jeff Quinnell running for two uncontested seats, Melby is in a strong position. 

“The community needs someone who is serious about doing this, and I didn’t want to leave a write-in to chance,” Melby said in an interview with The Olaf Messenger. 

While the sudden changes made to the ballot in early August are a cause of some excitement, Melby said she has no concerns regarding the civic stability of the Northfield community. 

“Initially the three incumbents, whose terms were up, all filed to run. I was very excited by this. It takes a lot of knowledge-building when you enter any elected position to understand the complexities of all that you’re going to run into,” Melby said. “When you have incumbents who file, there is some benefit to having this knowledge ready to go.” 

Miller, Quinnel and Melby’s combined knowledge will be especially beneficial for the upcoming term. Superintendent Tim Anderson is brand new to the position, and the district has nearly a 50% turnover rate in principal and leadership positions. The district also faces threats of nation-wide declining enrollment in K-12 schools, potentially leading to decreased state funding, which operates on a per-pupil basis. 

“When the dust settled and two of the three incumbents remained on the ballot, it seemed important we elect someone with knowledge and understanding of the complexity of the role,” Melby said. 

Melby served on Northfield Public Schools’ Legislative Action Committee for three years, where she learned about school funding mechanisms and the stress of unfunded mandates. 

Thus, maintaining financial health is one of Melby’s priorities moving forward, along with maintaining strong community engagement with families. 

“I have three kids in the school district in elementary, middle and high school, so I’m seeing the whole spectrum. While my kids have had a wonderful experience in the school district, I know that is not everyone’s experience,” Melby said. “I’m hoping to maintain the districts’ high level of community engagement by listening to parents’ concerns and considering where the board can take action.” 

On a more personal level, Melby said her final initiative is to reconsider the use of AI and technology in the classroom. 

“I have questions regarding the rapidity at which AI is infiltrating education at all levels, how we want teachers to address this and what policies we need to set at the district level to ensure ethical and appropriate usage,” Melby said. 

In her closing remarks, Melby was asked to consider the merit of building civic-mindedness at the college level. 

“Civic habits are built best when they’re built young,” Melby said. “I know both St. Olaf and Carleton College students are building their civic muscles on campus, sharing non-partisan voting resources and beyond.”

Just three weeks ago, St. Olaf College proudly welcomed 3,100 students back to the Hill, including a first-year population of 850 — the largest freshman class in St. Olaf history. While much of the student body was already eager to jump into their classes, it wouldn’t have been a true St. Olaf welcome without an extravagant welcome week. 

New Student Orientation (NSO) took place over the course of five days and was full of carefully crafted experiences meant to ease newcomers into the campus community — including but not limited to scavenger hunts meant to familiarize new students with the campus, randomized student groups to develop new friendships and elaborate parties to finish off the long, hot days. 

To learn more about the process of creating a successful welcome week, The Olaf Messenger interviewed Ryan Birnesser ’27, one of two student coordinators for NSO. When asked about the importance of student input when planning the week, Birnesser said, “I think it’s super valuable. The people in NSO do great things, but also, sometimes they don’t know what it’s like to experience NSO as a student … They need perspective from people who are going to say, ‘This is gonna be a long day.’” 

Birnesser also noted that the growing class sizes did not heavily contribute to any decisions made about NSO. Several notable changes, however, were made this year for St. Olaf Orientation to Academics and Resources (SOAR) and MORE groups. 

SOAR groups are divided by the first-year seminar, writing and rhetoric, or conversation program that new students choose to take during the fall semester. The groups consist of 10 to 20 students that meet every day during orientation week and periodically for the rest of the year. 

MORE groups are more focused on connecting students based on shared interests — incoming freshmen were placed into similarly sized groups of students who reported having the same interests. SOAR groups existed in years prior, but MORE groups are a recent addition, having been introduced just last year and expanded upon in 2026. SOAR group leaders have now shifted to focusing on providing students with resources and academic support. 

Madeleine Hayden ’30 and Micah Thompson ’30 reflected on the NSO experience in an interview with The Olaf Messenger. 

“If there had been opportunities for us to be physically introduced to resources instead of just told about them, it would’ve been more helpful,” Hayden said. This critique was aimed at the construction of SOAR groups, which incorporated education about campus resources and support but may have lacked the hands-on aspect of the learning experience. 

“I didn’t find the MORE groups fun,” Thompson said, noting that there was limited opportunity to meet new people organically. 

However, both students reported overall positive experiences with NSO and the evident care that was put into crafting the experience. 

The NSO committee will continue working to develop the orientation experience for future Oles.

content.rendered:
Former Minnesota Gov. Mark Dayton recently visited the Grand Event Center in downtown Northfield as part of a tour promoting his new memoir, “Perseverance.” 

Dayton, who served two terms through 2019, was previously state auditor and a U.S. senator. As governor, he signed same-sex marriage into law, raised the minimum wage, increased taxes on top earners and worked with lawmakers to fund the Minnesota Vikings’ billion-dollar stadium. 

His memoir, released Sept. 15, looks at the events and people that shaped his political life. He was joined by longtime friend Lori Sturdevant, a Star Tribune columnist and editor of his book, for a conversation about his decades in Minnesota politics. 

Jessica Peterson White, owner of Content Bookstore, which hosted the event, said she expected strong local interest as Minnesotans look back on Dayton’s time in office and prepare for another election.

“We’re here today, those of us who are hoping to kind of learn about where to go next,” Peterson White told The Olaf Messenger. 

Dayton has largely stayed out of the spotlight in recent years. However, as he approaches 80, he has begun to think about how he will be remembered.

“If I don’t tell my story my way, somebody else will tell it their way,” Dayton said. “It [‘Perseverance’] was a chance to look back on a career.”

The book’s title comes from what former U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy told Dayton early in his career: “Perseverance is the prerequisite for success in politics.”

“I think that’s true of most things in life,” Dayton said. “I hope the people reading this get nothing else out of it. They think ‘Yeah, I got to persevere.’” 

Early in the conversation, Dayton drew parallels between his days as a Vietnam War anti-war activist at Yale University and the current political climate. At the time, former President Richard Nixon had “all the power,” Dayton said.

While Dayton now spends much of the year in Arizona for health reasons, he said he watched in horror as Operation Metro Surge devastated the place where his “heart and soul” belonged.

“Vietnam was so appalling because you saw these innocent people being maimed, attacked,” he said. “But that was Americans attacking people in another country. These were Americans attacking Americans.” 

Dayton also acknowledged that Minnesota’s current politicians have a difficult road ahead of them, with inflation on the rise and a general lack of trust in government due to recent reports of fraud in state-managed social service and Medicaid programs. 

“I think we’re going to turn this country around, [and] to do that, you got to lead upward,” Dayton said. 

Sturdevant continued, noting that “what a governor candidate says in October matters in January and February if that candidate winds up being elected.” 

“[Political candidates] got to find out: what is our common cause? What are those matters that unite us?” Dayton said. “There’s got to be uplifting.”
